verdicts.title: Communication Lower Bounds via Critical Block Sensitivity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We use critical block sensitivity, a new complexity measure introduced by Huynh and Nordström (STOC 2012), to study the communication complexity of search problems. To begin, we give a simple new proof of the following central result of Huynh and Nordström: if $S$ is a search problem with critical block sensitivity $b$, then every randomised two-party protocol solving a certain two-party lift of $S$ requires $Ω(b)$ bits of communication. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses communication complexity, but it does not mention Ramanujan sums or minimal local indecomposable sheaf rank, which are central to the conjecture; it focuses on critical block sensitivity and its applications to monotone circuit depth and proof complexity.
